history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 3-week history of gradual onset headache and blurred vision, unresponsive to over-the-counter painkillers, and no fever, convulsions, or head trauma; she previously received presumptive antimalarial treatment and antibiotics without benefit.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient lives in a part of the world with a high HIV prevalence, and cryptococcal meningitis is the most common cause of adult meningitis in sub-Saharan Africa.
vitals: All vital signs are normal and she is afebrile.
physical_exam: The patient appears wasted and slightly anaemic, GCS is 15/15, no neck stiffness, normal visual acuity, and an abduction deficit of the left eye with 'blurring of vision' on left lateral gaze.
labs_and_diagnostics: Initial labs showed WBC 3.7 (×10^9/L), Haemoglobin 10.2 (g/dL), MCV 92 (fL), Platelets 91 (×10^9/L), Fasting blood glucose 5.43 (mmol/L), and negative Malaria RDT; CSF analysis revealed an opening pressure of 50 cmH2O, Leukocytes 18 (cells/µL), Protein 0.8 (g/L), Glucose 1.97 (mmol/L), negative India Ink, and C. neoformans on culture; HIV serology was positive with a CD4 count of 22/µL.
differential_diagnosis: Cryptococcal meningitis, tuberculous meningitis, and partially treated bacterial meningitis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was started on oral fluconazole 1200 mg and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, received repeated therapeutic lumbar punctures, and commenced antiretroviral therapy 4 weeks into antifungal treatment, but died 6 weeks later of an unknown cause.
